Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to get a clearer picture on two key items before we move to term discussions:

1) If GPU spot/market rates rise by >25% during our contract term, what options do we have for Luminary to get price protection or credit?
2) What discount bands are available for a 24-month committed pool at ~480 A100-equivalent hours/month (steady-state), and who needs to approve exceptions?

We'd like something we can show leadership that balances their risk tolerance with Redwood's operational constraints. I've attached our MAAP (usage projection) for context.

Can you propose a simple decision/trigger framework we can review — ideally with concrete numbers we can model?

Best,
Claire

Hi Claire — thanks for sending the MAAP. Quick reply and I pulled in ops & commercial: Marissa (pricing) and Karthik (capacity).

High level proposal (short):
- Base commitment: 24 months, 480 A100-eq hrs/mo steady-state
- Discount band: 18-22% off list for that commit band (final band determined after capacity allocation review)
- Price-safeguard trigger: if underlying GPU market index (Redwood GPU Index v1) increases >20% YoY for two consecutive quarters, Luminary can do one of the following (one-time, at trigger):
  a) Request a credit equal to 50% of the incremental per-token cost for the following quarter (applied as invoice credit), or
  b) Convert up to 20% of committed capacity to flexible (monthly billable at current market rate) with pro-rated credit applied to the remaining committed volume.

Approvals needed: any deviation from the 18-22% band or expanded credit beyond 50% requires pricing committee signoff (Marissa or her designated delegate) and ops confirmation that capacity pool is available.

I'll let Marissa and Karthik comment on feasibility & approval path — I kept this intentionally short so you can present a concrete ask to your leadership.

— Priyom
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Priyom / Karthik —
Forwarding a procurement note from Luminary. Quick internal read and answers below (copying essential bits into bullets).

Operational feasibility (Karthik):
- We can reserve a 480 A100-eq pool; needs a 30% buffer in the early ramp months (month 0-3) to protect against bursty inference patterns. Ops can commit to a phased activation schedule (70% ramp month1, 90% month2, 100% month3).
- Flexible conversion option (20%) is doable, but only if we keep a regional fallback pool — triggers must be region-aware (Luminary is US-first).

Commercial (Marissa):
- Discount band: we can start with 18% for standard review, 20% if Luminary signs a 30% upfront payment, 22% for 40%+ upfront and a firm Q4 campaign commitment.
- Credit structure: we can provision a 50% incremental-cost credit as you suggested, but we need a cap — recommend cap of $250k per year to bound exposure.
- Approval path: discounts >20% or credit cap >$250k escalate to Pricing Committee (me + CPO finance rep). Anything with re-pricing triggers tied to a 2-quarter index needs Legal review for precise wording.

Ask from internal side:
1) Priyom — can you convert the above into a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) that calls out the trigger metrics, sample math for Luminary's MAAP, and the fallback routing (region)? 2) Karthik — ops needs to confirm we can isolate a regional fallback pool for 20% flexible capacity and estimate the cost delta.

I'll be available for a quick sync Thurs 10am PT if helpful.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Pricing, Redwood Inference

Hi Claire — following our internal review, please find the proposed one-page MAP below (pasted) and the term-level asks. If Luminary is comfortable we can lock a draft term sheet and route to legal next week.

Mutual Action Plan (summary):
- Commitment: 24 months, 480 A100-eq hrs/mo steady-state (phase-in 70/90/100 over months 1-3).
- Commercial: 18% base discount. 20% with 30% upfront; 22% with 40%+ upfront + Q4 campaign.
- Price safeguard trigger: Redwood GPU Index up >20% YoY for 2 consecutive quarters.
  - Remedy A: 50% credit on incremental per-token cost for the following quarter (cap $250k/yr).
  - Remedy B: One-time conversion of up to 20% committed capacity to flexible monthly billing (pro-rated credit applied).
- Approval path: Discounts >20% or credit cap >$250k -> Pricing Committee (Marissa). Any index-linked contract language -> Legal review.
- Ops: Regional fallback pool required to enable 20% conversion; Redwood to confirm availability and cost delta in 48 hours.

Next steps requested from Luminary:
1) Confirm which remedy you prefer at trigger (A or B) — we can keep the other as fallback.
2) Indicate upfront payment appetite (none / 30% / 40%+) so we can finalize discount band.
3) Confirm target legal timeline (2-3 weeks preferred).

If this looks good I'll circulate a short term-sheet and route to legal. Happy to hop on a call if you prefer to walk through the math.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
